h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר כ״ח Pesach — Maamar Kaf Ches
Seven Days of Matzah, the Food of Healing, and Yechezkel's Dry Bones

p: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת לְמַעַן תִּזְכֹּר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ
"Seven days you shall eat matzos, in order that you may remember the day of your going forth from the land of Egypt all the days of your life"
(דְּבָרִים ט"ז, ג').
(Devarim 16:3).
וּבִפְשׁוּטוֹ אֵינוֹ מוּבָן: הֲלֹא נִצְטַוִּינוּ גַּם בְּכָל יוֹם לִזְכּוֹר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, וְלֹא נִצְטַוִּינוּ לֶאֱכוֹל שׁוּם דָּבָר לִרְמוֹז זֹאת!
Now in its plain sense this is not understood: surely we are also commanded every day of the year to remember the Exodus from Egypt, yet we are not commanded to eat anything to symbolize it!
גַּם לְהָבִין הָעִנְיָן שֶׁבְּפָרָשַׁת מִשְׁפָּטִים נִכְתַּב שַׁבָּת קוֹדֶם לְפֶסַח, וּבְפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא נִכְתַּב פֶּסַח קוֹדֶם לְשַׁבָּת
Also, we must understand why in Parshas Mishpatim Shabbos is written before Pesach, whereas in Parshas Ki Sisa Pesach is written before Shabbos
אַף דְּפֶסַח הָיָה מוּקְדָּם בַּזְּמַן לְשַׁבָּת, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הָא שַׁבָּת מְקוּדָּשׁ וְתָדִיר יוֹתֵר מִקְּדוּשַׁת יוֹם טוֹב, וְלוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַקְּדִימָה!
for even though Pesach preceded the formal command of Shabbos in time, nevertheless Shabbos is more sacred and more frequent than the holiness of Yom Tov, so by right it should take precedence!
וְהָעִנְיָן הוּא: דְּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
The explanation is that in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' קפ"ג:)
נִקְרָא מַצּוֹת "מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא",
matzos are called "the food of healing" (meichla d'asvasa),
וְהַיְינוּ דִּבְעֵת יְצִיאַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּצְרַיִם נִשְׁלַח הֶאָרָה בְּתוֹךְ לִבּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּלִי שׁוּם אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
meaning that at the time Israel went out of Egypt, an illumination was sent into the hearts of the Children of Israel without any prior awakening from below, as they said in the Midrash
(וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ"ג, ב'):
(Vayikra Rabbah 23:2):
הַלָּלוּ וְכוּלֵּי וְהַלָּלוּ וְכוּלֵּי
"These [were idolaters] and those [were idolaters], etc."

וְעַל זֶה נִצְטַוּוּ מִיָּד לֶאֱכוֹל שִׁבְעָה יָמִים מַצּוֹת, מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא, שֶׁיִּתְרַפְּאוּ מִכֹּל וָכֹל מִזּוֹהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ שֶׁבָּא גַּם כֵּן מִכֹּחַ אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע, וְזֶה הָיָה גַּם כֵּן הַכֹּל מֵאִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא.

and therefore they were immediately commanded to eat matzos—"the food of healing"—for seven days so that they would be completely healed from the filth of the Serpent, which had also entered through eating from the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, and this too came entirely from an awakening from above.
וְלָכֵן מַפְטִירִין בְּשַׁבָּת זוֹ בְּמֵתֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל:
And therefore on this Shabbos [of Chol HaMoed Pesach] we read the Haftarah of the dry bones revived by Yechezkel:
אַף דְּמָצִינוּ בְּטוּר אוֹרַח חַיִּים
for even though we find in the Tur, Orach Chaim
(סִימָן ת"צ)
(Siman 490)
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמָּסוֹרֶת בְּיָדָם שֶׁתְּחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים יִהְיֶה בְּפֶסַח, מִכָּל מָקוֹם לָמָּה דַּוְקָא בְּשַׁבָּת? הָיָה לָהֶם לְקוֹבְעָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב דְּפֶסַח עַצְמוֹ!

that it is because they have a tradition that the Resurrection of the Dead will take place on Pesach, nevertheless why specifically on Shabbos? They should have fixed it on the festival day of Pesach itself!
אַךְ יָדוּעַ דִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים יִהְיֶה עַל יְדֵי טַלָּא דְּנָטִיף מִלְּעֵילָּא מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא,
However, it is known that the Resurrection of the Dead will come about through the dew that drips from on high from Atika Kadisha,
וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַטַּלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא נִשְׁפָּע בְּשַׁבָּת קֹדֶשׁ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
and the root of the Dew of Atika Kadisha flows on the holy Shabbos, as brought in the holy Zohar
(חֵלֶק ב' פ"ח.):
וְהַאי יוֹמָא מַלְיָא רֵישָׁא דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין מִטַּלָּא דְּנָחִית מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא
"And on this day the head of Ze'ir Anpin is filled with the dew that descends from Atika Kadisha"
וְלָכֵן מַפְטִירִין דַּוְקָא בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַפֶּסַח, דְּהָא וְהָא גָּרְמוּ לְהַאי יוֹמָא.
and therefore we read it specifically on the Shabbos within Pesach, because both factors [Shabbos and Pesach] combine on this day.
וְרַשִׁ"י פֵּירֵשׁ
Now Rashi explained
(מְגִילָּה ל"א. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל בְּעַצְמוֹת)
(Megillah 31a, s.v. B'atzamos)
דִּלְכָךְ אָמַר רַב שָׁם דְּמַפְטִירִין בְּמֵתֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיוּ בְּנֵי אֶפְרַיִם שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִמִּצְרַיִם קוֹדֶם זְמַנָּם וְנֶהֶרְגוּ, וְיֵשׁ לָזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם.
that Rav stated there that we read the Haftarah of Yechezkel's dead because they were the Ephraimites who left Egypt prematurely and were slain, so this has a direct link to the Exodus from Egypt.
וְצָרִיךְ לוֹמַר דְּרַב לְשִׁיטָתֵיהּ דְּסוֹבֵר הָכִי
One must say that Rav follows his own opinion, as he holds this view
(סַנְהֶדְרִין צ"ב:)
(Sanhedrin 92b)
דְּהֵם הָיוּ בְּנֵי אֶפְרַיִם;
that they were the Ephraimites;

אַךְ לִשְׁאָר אָמוֹרָאִים שָׁם דְּסָבְרוּ שֶׁהָיוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בָּהֶם לַחְלוּחִית שֶׁל מִצְוָה וְשֶׁכָּפְרוּ בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, וְלֹא מָצִינוּ דִּפְלִיגִי הָכָא בְּעִנְיַן הַפְטָרָה דְּמֵתֵי יְחֶזְקֵאל

yet according to the other Amoraim there, who held that they were people devoid of any moisture of mitzvos or who denied the Resurrection of the Dead—and we do not find that they dispute the Haftarah of Yechezkel's dead
וּלְפִי רֶמֶז הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל גַּם לְשִׁיטָתָם יֵשׁ בָּזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת לִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם:
according to the allusion explained above, even on their view there is a direct connection to the Exodus from Egypt:

כִּי עִיקַּר הָרֶמֶז הוּא עַל שֶׁבִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא לְהוֹשִׁיעַ כָּל פְּרָטֵי נַפְשׁוֹת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אַף שֶׁנִּטְבְּעוּ בְּעוֹמֶק הַקְּלִיפָּה וּלְפִי רְאוּת עֵינָם אֵין לָהֶם שׁוּם תִּקְוָה, רַק הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּרוֹב רַחֲמָיו הוֹצִיאָם

for the core allusion is that at the Exodus from Egypt there was an awakening from above to save every individual soul of Israel, even though they were submerged in the depths of the husk and in their own eyes had no hope whatsoever, yet the Holy One, blessed is He, in His abundant mercy brought them out
כְּמוֹ כֵן בְּכָל שָׁנָה בְּאוֹתוֹ הַזְּמַן מִתְנוֹצֵץ הֶאָרָה זוֹ מִטַּלָּא דְּנָחִית מִלְּעֵילָּא,
and similarly every year at this very time, this illumination sparkles forth from the dew descending from on high,
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בִּיחֶזְקֵאל
and this is what is written there in Yechezkel
(ל"ז, י"א-י"ב):
אֲשֶׁר אָמְרוּ לְנַפְשָׁם: יָבְשׁוּ עַצְמוֹתֵינוּ אָבְדָה תִקְוָתֵנוּ... כֹּה אָמַר ה': הִנֵּה אֲנִי פֹתֵחַ אֶת קִבְרוֹתֵיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר
"Who say to themselves, 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost'... Thus says Hashem: 'Behold, I am opening your graves, etc.'"

שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת מֵיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא מִתְעוֹרֵר בְּכָל שָׁנָה בְּאוֹתוֹ זְמַן לְהַעֲבִיר זוֹהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ וּלְתַקֵּן פְּגַם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁגָּרַם מִיתָה לָעוֹלָם, וּמִמֵּילָא יְבוּלַּע הַמָּוֶת לָנֶצַח וְיִזְכּוּ לִתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים שֶׁבָּא עַל יְדֵי טַלָּא דְּעַתִּיקָא.

meaning that through eating the "food of healing" [matzah], an awakening occurs every year at this season to remove the filth of the Serpent and rectify the primordial blemish that brought death into the world, so that death will automatically be swallowed up forever and they will merit the Resurrection of the Dead that comes through the Dew of Atika.
וְאַף שֶׁאֵין אָנוּ מַרְגִּישִׁים שׁוּם רְפוּאָה וּפְעוּלָּה, אַף עַל פִּי כֵן בְּוַדַּאי הוּא פּוֹעֶלֶת מְעַט מְעַט כְּמוֹ כָּל הָרְפוּאוֹת הַגּוּפָנִיּוֹת שֶׁפּוֹעֲלִים מְעַט מְעַט.
And even though we do not consciously feel any healing or effect, nevertheless it certainly works gradually, little by little, just like all physical medicines that act incrementally.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: שִׁבְעַת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת, הַמֵּיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא, לְמַעַן תִּזְכֹּר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם
And this is what is meant by "Seven days you shall eat matzos"—the food of healing—"in order that you may remember the day of your going forth from the land of Egypt"

הַיְינוּ שֶׁתִּזְכּוֹר וְתַרְגִּישׁ "יוֹם צֵאתְךָ", הָאוֹר שֶׁבָּא אֵלֶיךָ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מִצַּד אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא, שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְשׁוּקָּעִים אָז בְּאַרְבָּעִים וְתֵשַׁע שַׁעֲרֵי טוּמְאָה כַּיָּדוּעַ;

meaning that you remember and experience "the day of your going forth," the light that came to you on that day through an awakening from above when Israel were sunk in the forty-nine gates of impurity, as is known;

פֶּסַח מְרַמֵּז "פֶּה סָח", שֶׁהָיָה הַדִּיבּוּר בְּגָלוּת, וּבִיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם פָּתַח ה' פִּיּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיּוּכְלוּ לְדַבֵּר לְפָנָיו כְּעֶבֶד שֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְדַבֵּר לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,

for Pesach alludes to Peh Sach ("a mouth that speaks"), because speech had been in exile, and at the Exodus from Egypt Hashem opened the mouths of the Children of Israel so they could speak before Him like a slave granted permission to speak before the king,
וְזֶה הוּא עִנְיַן סְמִיכוּת גְּאוּלָּה לִתְפִלָּה, דְּמָצִינוּ
and this is the essence of juxtaposing Redemption to Prayer, as we find
(בְּרָכוֹת ט':)
(Berachos 9b)
בְּרַב בְּרוּנָא דְּלָא פְּסַק חוּכָא מִפּוּמֵיהּ,
regarding Rav Beruna, from whose mouth laughter did not cease [all day after joining Redemption to Prayer],
הַיְינוּ שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר הִשְׁלִים בִּרְכוֹת הַגְּאוּלָּה שֶׁמְּסַיֵּים "אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח" דִּכְגְאוּלָּה אֲרוּכָה דָּמְיָא
meaning that when one completes the blessings of Redemption and concludes with "My Lord, open my lips," which is considered an extended redemption
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם),
(as they said there),
וְאָז כְּשֶׁנִּיתַּן לוֹ רְשׁוּת יוּכַל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל לְפָנָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ.
then, once granted permission, he can pray before Him, blessed be His Name.

וְלָכֵן בְּפָרָשַׁת כִּי תִשָּׂא כְּתִיב פֶּסַח קוֹדֶם שַׁבָּת, דְּזָכוּ לִקְדוּשַׁת הַשַּׁבָּת הַכֹּל עַל יְדֵי יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בְּפֶסַח וְעַל יְדֵי הַמֵּיכְלָא דְּאַסְוָותָא מִצַּד אִתְּעָרוּתָא דִּלְעֵילָּא;

And therefore in Parshas Ki Sisa [which was given after the Golden Calf], Pesach is written before Shabbos, because they merited the holiness of Shabbos entirely through the Exodus from Egypt on Pesach and through the "food of healing" via an awakening from above;
אֲבָל בְּפָרָשַׁת מִשְׁפָּטִים, שֶׁנִּכְתַּב אַחַר מַתַּן תּוֹרָה קוֹדֶם הַקִּלְקוּל, דִּבְשַׁעַת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה כְּבָר פָּסְקָה זוֹהֲמָתָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת

whereas in Parshas Mishpatim, which was written after the Giving of the Torah and prior to the sin of the Golden Calf—for at the Giving of the Torah their filth had already ceased, as they said in Shabbos
וְאָז נֶאֱמַר
and then it was said
(תְּהִלִּים פ"ב, ו'):
(Tehillim 82:6):
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי וְגוֹמֵר וּבְנֵי עֶלְיוֹן כֻּלְּכֶם וְגוֹמֵר,
"I said, etc., and sons of the Most High are you all, etc.,"
דְּלָא הֲווֹ מַיְיתֵי
so that they would not die
(עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה'.)
(Avodah Zarah 5a)
לֹא נִצְרְכוּ אָז לְרֶמֶז זֶה, לָכֵן שָׁם נִכְתַּב שַׁבָּת קוֹדֶם לְפֶסַח, דְּתָדִיר וּמְקוּדָּשׁ קוֹדֶם.
they did not need this allusion then, and therefore there Shabbos is written before Pesach, because that which is more frequent and more sacred takes precedence.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Machshavos Charutz 7 — “Reading the section of the Heifer works to bring this into the heart little by little, before Pesach, so that through it we may merit on Pesach the revival of the dead that will be on Pesach; that is why on Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach we read as haftarah the dry bones. It seems to me that the revival of the dead will be on the Shabbos within Pesach, like the Giving of the Torah, which was on Shabbos, when the dew of revival also descended.” Connection: It also ties the dry-bones haftarah to the meeting of Pesach and Shabbos, and adds that the revival itself will come on the Shabbos within Pesach, as the dew of revival fell at Sinai on Shabbos.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shabbos Chol HaMoed Pesach 14 — “Hashem showed him that there is no place in Israel wholly empty of light. He showed it through these dry bones, whose whole sin was that they erred in reckoning the end. Even this error was not wholly empty of the light of His will: Hashem had begun to reckon the end, but they did not wait until He finished and went out a little early. So all their sin was that they ate unripe fruit. And this is what Hashem said: ‘These bones are the whole house of Israel’: as the sin of these bones, so is the sin of all Israel.” Connection: It finds in the dry bones hope for those who seem past hope, and adds that the Ephraimites’ sin, like every sin in Israel, was only haste.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Tzvi Elimelech of Dinov, Bnei Yissaschar, Maamarei Chodesh Nisan, Maamar 4:5 — “The Zohar calls matzah ‘the bread of healing’; which illness does it heal? Man was made upright and wholly good, and was commanded not to eat from the Tree of Knowledge, for through it evil would enter him. Since he transgressed at the counsel of the Samekh-Mem who rode upon the serpent, his material being grew coarse and evil entered it, until it had to be consumed through death, the wound of the whole world. Hashem commanded us matzah, guarded from chametz, which raises up coarseness like that evil; this is a sign of the nullifying of that power, until death is swallowed up forever. Therefore matzah is called the bread of healing, a cure and remedy for the wound of the world.” Connection: Bnei Yissaschar likewise makes matzah the cure for the serpent's poison of the Tree of Knowledge, whose end is the swallowing of death; he adds that chametz itself embodies that swelling evil.
